clue.text: Top Belgium international ignored by Redknapp, maybe

indicators.note: what is ignored gets left out, so one letter is dropped from the name that follows

blocks.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
Louise Redknapp is a British pop singer, once of the group Eternal; 'maybe' flags her as one Redknapp among several
I is a standard abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A star Belgian footballer is snubbed by the pundit or manager Redknapp.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface points to Harry or Jamie Redknapp, but the Redknapp needed is Louise, the singer; drop the I from LOUISE and put B in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A blouse is a loose shirt-like garment worn on the upper body, which clothing shops call a top.

clue.text: Fruit cakes beginning to deteriorate in large handkerchief

indicators.note: to cake is to coat or encase, so one piece is wrapped around another
the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a banana is a fruit
the opening letter

explanation.surface: Fruitcakes start to go off when wrapped in a big hanky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit cakes' looks like one baked item; split it, and 'cakes' is a verb meaning encases.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandana is a big square of patterned cloth tied around the head or neck, essentially an oversized kerchief.

clue.text: Concerning number withdrawing flat cola bottles

indicators.note: to bottle is to hold inside a container, so the letters sit within these words
withdrawing is drawing back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A drinker is worried that flat cola bottles are being recalled.
explanation.walkthrough: Read upwards in this down clue the letters spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Octal describes the base-eight counting system, so it is an adjective relating to a way of writing numerals.

clue.text: Revolutionary sects primarily infiltrated an island nation

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the letters are turned back to front
primarily means first of all, so the opening letters are taken

blocks.note: cults are religious sects
the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: Rebel religious groups penetrated a small island state.
explanation.walkthrough: The ST stands for Saint, so the enumeration splits as two letters then five.
explanation.definitionFit: St Lucia is a sovereign Caribbean country occupying a single island in the Windward chain.

clue.text: Endless Swiss chocolate not ultimately beneficial for heavenly body

indicators.note: without ends means both the first and last letters are cut away
saying a thing is not present means taking that letter out of the word
ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter is wanted

blocks.note: Toblerone is the triangular Swiss chocolate bar; without its ends it leaves these letters
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone claims a trimmed-down Toblerone isn't good for your body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly body' plays on 'body' in a health sense; the chocolate loses both ends and then its L.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is one of the moons of Uranus, and any moon counts as a celestial object in space.

clue.text: Oddly, beetle and fish found in part of steeple

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions: first, third, fifth

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters
fry are young fish

explanation.surface: Strangely, a beetle and a fish turn up inside a church tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' reads as strangely, but here it selects the odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The belfry is the chamber of a church tower where the bells hang, a section of the spire structure.

clue.text: Denial of unhappiness with leader becoming Republican

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, and becoming means it is swapped for something else

blocks.note: dejection is low spirits
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Political sadness is denied once a Republican takes over as leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening D for R.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal or dismissal of a request is a rejection, and a denial in that sense means the same.

clue.text: Japanese drama show with singing finishing early a complete failure

indicators.note: finishing early means stopping short, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: Noh is classical Japanese masked theatre
opera is drama set to singing

explanation.surface: A Japanese stage show with songs that ends early is a total flop.
explanation.walkthrough: Noh is the stately masked theatre of Japan, a crossword favourite because of its short spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is a person with no chance of success, informally a total loser.

clue.text: Pete Tong spins wrong song by Duffy

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of place and must be rearranged into the right order

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: The DJ Pete Tong plays the wrong record by Duffy.
explanation.walkthrough: Pete Tong is a famous Radio 1 DJ and also rhyming slang for wrong; 'spins' sounds like his job but belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepping Stone was a 2008 single by the Welsh singer Duffy, from her album Rockferry.

clue.text: Forcefully strike the wrong way, resulting in tie

indicators.note: going the wrong way means travelling backwards, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to tonk is British slang for to hit hard

explanation.surface: A batter mistimes a big hit and the match ends level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tie' looks like a drawn match after the sporting 'strike', but it means a fastening. TONK is informal British for a hefty blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Tying a rope or string produces a fastening loop, so a noun meaning a tie in that physical sense fits.

clue.text: Robin Hood's friend is potty?

blocks.note: surface reading: one of the Merry Men of Sherwood Forest, the giant ironically nicknamed for his size
setter's reading: a potty is a small toilet, and 'john' is American slang for a lavatory

explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' seems to mean crazy, as if gossiping about the outlaw; read it as a child's chamber pot, a small lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: The outlaw's sidekick is named exactly, and the name also reads as a diminutive toilet, matching a child's potty.

clue.text: Periodically Grace left in charge of language

indicators.note: something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters
L is the usual abbreviation for left
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Grace is put in charge of teaching a language from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' looks like it describes how often Grace is in charge, but it picks letters from her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaelic is the Celtic tongue spoken in parts of Scotland and Ireland, so it is a language by name.

clue.text: Bible passage disheartened observer, in the main

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the central letter, the heart of the word

blocks.note: a submarine's viewing tube watches from beneath the main, the sea

explanation.surface: A gloomy watcher at sea reads a passage of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old word for the open sea. The nine-letter observer loses its middle letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: A pericope is a selected extract of scripture read aloud in church services, a technical term for an excerpt.

clue.text: President's retreat affected fanatical Dutch bores

indicators.note: to bore is to drill a hole into, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: camp means theatrical or affected in manner
avid means keen to the point of obsession
D is the abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: Pretentious, obsessive Dutch people drive the president away in boredom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bores' reads as wearies, but it means drills into: D goes inside AVID.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp David is the country retreat in Maryland used by US presidents for rest and summit meetings.

clue.text: Perhaps tapir rhymed with 'cap queer'

indicators.note: queer in its old sense means odd or strange, so the letters are put in an odd new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet rhymes 'tapir' with the phrase 'cap queer'.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks suggest a rhyme being reported; 'queer' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The tapir is a thick-skinned hoofed mammal traditionally grouped with elephants and rhinos as an example of this class.

clue.text: Tramp removed from more uneven seaside attraction

indicators.note: what is removed from a word is taken out of it, leaving the rest behind

blocks.note: a bum is a vagrant
bumpier means rougher, less even

explanation.surface: A vagrant is moved on from an increasingly rough seafront amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: BUM is the American word for a tramp, and it happens to be the first three letters of the comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: British resorts have long walkways built out over the sea, with arcades, which count as a classic holiday draw.

clue.text: Mark wonderful staff

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for the German mark currency
ace is informal for excellent

explanation.surface: Someone rates their employees highly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees but is a ceremonial rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is an ornamental rod carried as a symbol of authority in parliaments and processions.

clue.text: Space to turn in good parking space

indicators.note: turning round makes something face the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: room means space
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A driver needs room to turn in a decent parking spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parking space' suggests a car, but a boat is parked too.
explanation.definitionFit: A mooring is a berth where a boat is tied up, the waterborne equivalent of a spot for leaving a vehicle.

clue.text: Try to stop strangely anaemic Donald Trump?

definitions.note: an example, signalled by the question mark

indicators.note: something arranged strangely is out of its normal order, so these letters are rearranged
a stopper plugs the middle of something, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: An attempt to halt a strangely pale Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try to stop' reads as a plea to block Trump; instead the word for an attempt is the stopper, plugged inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Trump is famous for self-promotion, so he is offered as an example of someone obsessed with himself.

clue.text: After returning, rarely bored by university course sections

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters go in reverse
to be bored by is to be drilled into, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: seldom means rarely
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A returning student is seldom bored by their university course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bored' suggests tedium, but it means drilled into: U goes inside the backwards adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Degree programmes are divided into separately taught units, and each such unit is called a module.

clue.text: Cooked rarebit for judge

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone makes Welsh rarebit, cheese on toast, to serve a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is a British dish of melted cheese on toast; its seven letters are simply rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is a person appointed to settle a dispute, an adjudicator with authority to decide.

clue.text: Mishit crossing centre of defunct drain

indicators.note: to cross something is to span it, so one piece lies across and around the other
the centre of a word is its middle letter

blocks.note: a slice is a golf shot that curves off line
the middle letter of a seven-letter word

explanation.surface: A wayward golf shot sails over the middle of a disused drain.
explanation.walkthrough: A slice is a golf shot that curls away to the side, the classic mishit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sluice is a channel with a gate for controlling water, so it serves as a drain or outlet.

clue.text: Multilingual parrot obtained with more eastern languages, originally

indicators.note: east lies to the right on a map, so a letter shifts further along the word

blocks.note: Polly is the stock name for a pet parrot
got means obtained
the initial L identifies which letter of the parrot is moved

explanation.surface: A parrot that speaks several tongues is acquired along with more Eastern languages.
explanation.walkthrough: Write POLLY then GOT, and move one L, the first letter of languages, further east, that is rightward, into GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyglot is a person who speaks several tongues, and the word also works as an adjective with that sense.

clue.text: Main course in Europe is meat stew with bit of nutmeg in

indicators.note: a small bit of a word is one letter, here the first
with something in means holding it inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: a daube is a French braised meat stew
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A European restaurant's main course is a meat stew seasoned with nutmeg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main course' sounds like a dinner, but a course is the path of a river, the main channel of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danube flows across central Europe to the Black Sea, so it is a major waterway on that continent.

clue.text: Raised on booze in country

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, and in a down entry reading upward runs the letters backwards

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
gin is alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone brought up on drink in a particular country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised on booze' reads as a childhood story; in a down clue it means write RE and GIN, then read them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked West African state, a sovereign nation named after its great river.

clue.text: By one, Fritz possibly recalled old Rugby broadcast?

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters come back in the opposite order

blocks.note: as in multiplication: three by four is three times four
the Roman numeral for one
Fritz Lang was the director of Metropolis; 'possibly' marks him as one Fritz

explanation.surface: A German named Fritz remembers an old rugby match on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is not the sport but the English town whose radio transmitter long broadcast the national time signal, hence 'old' and the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rugby transmitter sent out the official British clock pulses, so its broadcast was a precise time-keeping transmission.

clue.text: Picked up pace to make entrance

indicators.note: a sound picked up is heard by the ear, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a gait is a manner of walking, a pace

explanation.surface: Someone hurries along to make a grand entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up pace' reads as sped up; split it as a sound heard plus the word for a walking style.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate is a hinged barrier in a fence or wall that provides a way in, an opening.

clue.text: German writer's allowed boring item

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for German
the writer of a clue is 'I', so 'the writer is' becomes I'M
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A German author is permitted a tedious object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' seems to mean dull, but it means drilling holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A gimlet is a small hand tool with a screw tip for drilling holes in wood, so it does boring.

clue.text: Moneylender texted "You're certain to be included"

indicators.note: what is included is put inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: text-message shorthand writes you're as U R
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A loan shark sends a text assuring someone they are bound to be part of the deal.
explanation.walkthrough: In text-speak 'you're' shrinks to the two letters U R, which wrap around the word for certain.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends cash at exorbitant interest, a pejorative term for a lender of funds.
